title: What does DIDSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DIDSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DIDSet creates or updates an account's decentralized identifier and associated references. [1]

DIDDocument, URI and Data provide different ways to carry or reference identifier information within the transaction's limits. A DID helps publish an identity relationship but does not itself perform customer due diligence. Check controller authority and current resolution. A pointer to a document is not a ledger guarantee that its claims are accurate or its host remains available. [1]

The DIDSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using DIDSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
